entry.title: Dancing to one of my fav songs | #bharatanatyam #dance #arrahman #carnaticraga #karanas

media:group.media:title: Dancing to one of my fav songs | #bharatanatyam #dance #arrahman #carnaticraga #karanas
Backstage and improv | Rukmini Vijayakumar #bharatanatyam #dance #improvisation #stageshow
media:group.media:description:
Improvisation is an inherent part of classical Indian dance and music-and one of its most beautiful aspects. You can truly explore it as a dancer only when you share the stage with a live ensemble of musicians.
We work with a skeletal structure-traditional norms of tala, placement of teermanams, muktāyams, swaras-but how the abhinaya, the story, and the musicality unfold happens in that shared moment between performers and audience.
The short jathi in this video was composed by @shyam_rhythmgam just a day before the show, with @konnakkolsomashekarjois adding his own interpretation. I had heard it only a few times before dancing it on stage. What I danced may not have been perfect-but it was born in that moment, in response to what I was hearing.
Most of Saturday night was like this. I responded to @raghuram_rajagopalan 's voice as I created the worlds of Krishna, Yashoda, and the Gopikas in Amma Nănu, the devotion of the final abhang, and the jealousy of Devyani in the varnam-with @nithishammannaya guiding the emotional landscape on the flute.
All of it was new to us. And without videos, these moments would live only in memory-in the bodies of dancers, in the hearts of musicians, and with the audience-until they surface again in performance.
I don't want to choreograph every moment of abhinaya or nritta. Once I become Devyani, Krishna, or Yashoda, I respond to the world they inhabit in that moment. That freedom is everything to me. This is the beauty of having live musicians on stage-and I would never trade it for a "perfect" performance. Thank you for sharing Saturday evening with me at @heritageparampara, Gudiya Sambhrama Festival. And thank you for all the messages-they remind me how powerful dance is, and how grateful I am for this language.
(Some tiny clips that @ramyakadambi could capture while backstage)

media:group.media:title: Protect me Devi | #bharatanatyam #devi #vedanta #goddess #surrender #dancer
media:group.media:description:
When the lyrics say " protect me oh Devi, I have no one else but you" something always stirs inside me. That there is and will always be only one refuge.... That singular divinity that we surrender to.
I know there aren't any lyrics in this music because it's instrumental, but the lyrics run in my mind when I'm improvising
Beautiful music by@anilsrinivasan & @lalgudi_krishnan
